thread:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: SEV2 alert: high 502/timeout rate from northamerica-central1 egress (NAT pool 3). Detected 11:57 UTC, error spike to 8% p50 latency ↑ 350ms. Pager routed to oncall. Auto-escalation threshold passed. Link: https://ops.redwood.internal/incidents/2112233445

Alex O'Neill (oncall): I'm on it. initial triage: 11:58 UTC - seeing repeated `NAT_CONN_RESET` in /var/log/egress-proxy. Trying to confirm whether this is network flap or pool exhaustion.

Samir Patel: Confirmed flow logs show heavy SYN_RETRY for nodes in nac-central1-b. CPU on gateway nodes is normal, socket tables nearing capacity. Could be ephemeral port exhaustion on the NAT gateway.

Tia Gomez (sre): Good call. If it's port exhaustion we should trigger immediate fallback to cross-region egress and enable new ephemeral port allocation. Steps: - scale up gateway pool (gateway-pool-3) by +2 instances - enable `egress.cross_region_fallback=true` for affected route group.

Alex O'Neill: Scaling gateway-pool-3 now. Running: ```gcloud compute instances resize gateway-pool-3 --size=+2 --zone=nac-central1-b``` Will watch metrics.

DeployBot: Resize job queued: job-id=resize-211223-01. ETA ~45s.

Samir Patel: While scaling I pushed a temporary kernel param on the gateways to increase local port range: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="15000 61000"` and `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1` — applying via salt on pool nodes. This should immediately increase ephemeral ports.

Tia Gomez: Routing change ready. Preparing to flip `egress.cross_region_fallback` for customer-facing routes in `nac-central1`. Will set to `true` for route groups: r-gen, r-emb, r-rerank.

Alex O'Neill: Traffic started rerouting at 12:01 UTC. Error rate dropping to 2.1% now. Latency p50 back to 130ms. Still watching.

Joe Park (eng-runtime): Quick note — cross-region fallback will increase token egress cost for affected requests ~1.8x. Heads up for billing/ops to monitor. Also verifying model-serving compatibility when routed (we have a fallback mapping to the same model family).

Elena Ruiz (product): Drafting customer heads-up note. Will post to status page once we have stable mitigation.

Samir Patel: Resize succeeded, kernel params applied, fallback toggled. Observability: `egress_conn_reset` events dropping, SYN_RETRY rate normalized.

IncidentBot: Update at 12:07 UTC: mitigation in progress — cross-region fallback enabled, gateway pool scaled. Incident state: PARTIALLY_MITIGATED.

Alex O'Neill: I'm going to spin a short status page update. Draft below — please sign off: 

"We are currently investigating elevated request errors (502/timeouts) impacting customers in northamerica-central1. We've routed traffic to alternate egress endpoints and scaled gateway capacity to reduce impact. Customers may see transient increases in latency while traffic stabilizes. Root cause is suspected ephemeral port exhaustion on regional NAT gateways; further updates will be provided as we confirm recovery and next steps."

Tia Gomez: LGTM, add estimated ETA to full recovery: ~30-45 minutes.

Elena Ruiz: Customer notification template (short): 

"Short update — We are mitigating an issue affecting API requests from the northamerica-central1 region. We have routed traffic to alternative egress endpoints and scaled infrastructure; errors are decreasing. We will follow up with a detailed post-incident summary. If you have specific customers impacted, please reply with customer names/IDs and we'll prioritize communication."

Joe Park: Add note: if customers have strict geo restrictions (IP allowlists), they may see failures because traffic will egress from different IP ranges. Recommend Ops send a targeted list to accounts.

Alex O'Neill: Noted. @Elena please add that line. Also tagging @Samir to collect per-customer hit counts: `SELECT customer_id, count(*) FROM requests WHERE region='nac-central1' AND http_status IN (502,504) AND ts >= '2026-03-15T11:45:00Z' GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 20;`

Samir Patel: Running query now, will paste top-affected customers in ~5m.

IncidentBot: Alert: new related alarm — NAT pool 3 socket table utilization 95% (resolved after scale).

Alex O'Neill: We're at 12:23 UTC — errors at 0.6%, latency returned to baseline for most tenants. I'll keep the cross-region fallback in place for another hour to ensure stability, then revert with canary.

Tia Gomez: Agreed. Plan for rollback: 1) monitor 30m, 2) gradually reduce gateway pool back to baseline, 3) disable fallback in canary groups for 10% of traffic, 4) if stable, full revert. I'll own the rollback play and post timeline.

Elena Ruiz: Status page posted (Incident 2112233445): https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2112233445 — short notice sent to customers. Copy of notification pinned here: "We routed traffic to alternate egress to mitigate elevated errors. Some customers with IP allowlists may experience issues; contact support if needed."

Samir Patel: Top affected customers (pre-mitigation): `cust_4582 (420 errors), cust_991 (310), cust_1201 (140)`. Re-running for the 12:00-12:25 window for short report.

Joe Park: Can we add a medium-term mitigation to prevent recurrence: increase ephemeral port range on all gateway images by default + alert on socket table >75%? Put a task in infra backlog and link to incident.

Alex O'Neill: Filing infra ticket now: INFRA-2103 "increase default ephemeral ports & socket table alerting" and linking incident id.

IncidentBot: Incident state changed to RESOLVED (mitigation held) at 12:40 UTC. Post-incident review and timeline required.

Tia Gomez: I'll coordinate postmortem draft. Owners: SRE (Tia), Network (Samir), Runtime (Joe). Targeting completed draft in 48 hours.

Elena Ruiz: Will follow-up on customer comms with affected accounts, attach the full timeline and next steps.

Alex O'Neill: Thanks all — I'll keep the rollback schedule pinned. If anything flares, re-pager. :thumbsup:

DeployBot: Cleanup jobs queued: resize-revert INFRA-rollback-211223 when requested.

IncidentBot: Thread closed for active mitigation notes. Please add follow-ups to the incident tracker."
